subject: Re: Post-call: integration & routing requirements for model serving
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.io>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: integration & routing requirements

Thanks again for the call this morning - great to meet you both. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary (from today's discovery):
- Primary use case: product search augmentation + contextual chat inside Acme's support console.
- Traffic profile: ~100 qps baseline, spikes to ~500 qps during business hours.
- Latency target (UX): ideally <100ms token latency for interactive snippets, but Acme mentioned they can tolerate up to 200ms for now.
- Data & compliance: must be deployed in a US-only VPC; logs/audit trail retention policy needed.
- Cost sensitivity: want to optimize for unit cost on embeddings/rerank while keeping a high-quality generator for chat.

Key technical items we discussed to confirm:
1) SDK and auth: you prefer a quick SDK drop-in + mTLS or API-key flows for service-to-service calls.
2) Routing & policies: need region-aware routing, latency/cost policy rules, and a fallback chain when primary model capacity is constrained.
3) Structured output & tool calling: chat will use structured JSON responses and callouts to internal search tool for reranking.
4) Embeddings & reranker pipeline: embeddings for semantic search + reranker model to rescore top-k candidates.

Attachments: sharing a short mutual action plan (MAP) + a high-level SLA/architecture diagram for how Redwood would handle routing/autoscale (see attached).

Proposed next steps:
- Acme: confirm VPC constraints, data residency contact, and preferred auth (mTLS vs API key) - Jordan/Priya
- Redwood: internal eng to propose a routing config and sample SDK snippet; propose a technical deep-dive with Dev and Marcus next week
- Schedule: can we lock a 60-min pairing session on Wed 6/16 or Thu 6/17?

If this matches your notes, I'll have Dev draft a sample routing-config and a short checklist for SDK setup ahead of the pairing call.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

--

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: integration & routing requirements

Thanks Marissa, that lines up with our notes. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- VPC requirement: correct, all inference traffic must be inside our US-only VPC; we run additional network ACLs. We will need a short checklist for network setup and any ports to allow for the private control plane.
- Auth: security team prefers mTLS for service-to-service. We can do API keys for sandbox but production should be mTLS.
- Latency: our product team pushed back on <100ms; they say 200ms is acceptable for phase 1. Important: p95 for end-to-end response should not exceed 500ms.
- Embeddings: ranking pipeline needs embeddings computed and stored in our vector DB (we use Pinecone). We'll need a predictable QPS for embedding writes (expect 100-200 writes/minute during sync jobs).

We'd like to see:
1) a sample routing-config that shows fallback chains (e.g., redwood-gpt-1 -> redwood-llm-slim -> local-onprem-fallback) and cost/latency policy thresholds,
2) SDK sample for auth + streaming responses, and
3) an outline for the reranker integration (input/outputs expected).

Happy to take the pairing session, Thu 6/17 10am PT works for us. Also can share our security contact (Priya) to take a SOC2 questionnaire.

Jordan
Senior Product Manager, Acme Corporation

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme.io>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: integration & routing requirements

Thanks Jordan, good constraints to have. I sketched a pragmatic configuration and notes below to speed the deep-dive. I attached a routing-config-example.yaml that mirrors this description.

High-level approach (short):
- SDK/auth: recommend using our client SDK with mTLS for prod and API keys for sandbox. SDK can be initialized with a cert + key and will do automatic token refresh for control-plane ops. We provide examples for Node/Python/Go.

- Model routing & policy primitives:
  * routes: logical endpoints (e.g., /chat, /search-embed, /rerank)
  * policy rules: latency_target_ms, max_cost_per_token_usd, preferred_region, fallback_chain
  * example rule: for /chat set latency_target_ms=200, preferred_region=us-east-1, fallback_chain=[gpt-4x, gpt-3.5-slim] with cost threshold $0.001/token

- Fallback behavior: if primary model's queue latency > latency_target_ms OR model unavailable, route to next in fallback_chain. We also support partial response streaming from fallback if primary stalls.

- Region routing: requests arrive at control plane (in your US VPC), then we select region-aware serving pools. Policy can be strict (deny cross-region) or soft (route to lower-cost region if latency within threshold). Example: prefer us-east-1, allow us-west-2 if p95 latency delta < 50ms.

- Embedding + reranker flow:
  1) Embedding service: batch writes to Pinecone; we recommend async writes with a small queue and backpressure knobs.
  2) Reranker: candidate generation from vector DB (top-50) -> reranker model scores -> top-5 returned. We support hosting reranker as a lightweight CPU model or a small GPU for latency-sensitive scoring.

- Structured output/tool calling: use our function-calling structured output mode; define a JSON schema for tool responses. SDK will validate and surface tool-call intents. For search calls, you can request both "tools: [search]" and a structured "response_schema: {...}" so your UI gets typed output.

- Observability + failover: tracing and token-level cost in the Console; include per-route dashboards and automatic fallback alerts when fallbacks increase above X%.

Sample routing-config (excerpt):
# routing-config-example.yaml
routes:
  - name: chat
    endpoint: /v1/chat
    policy:
      latency_target_ms: 200
      max_cost_per_token_usd: 0.001
      preferred_region: us-east-1
      fallback_chain: [redwood-gpt-4x, redwood-llm-slim]
  - name: search-embed
    endpoint: /v1/embeddings
    policy:
      preferred_region: us-east-1
      batching: auto
      max_batch_size: 256

Next steps from engineering side:
- I'll drop the routing-config-example.yaml in the shared Drive and bring an SDK sample to the pairing call.
- For mTLS onboarding we'll provide a short checklist: cert format, trust anchor, connection port, and IP allowlist.

If this looks good, I'll join the Thu 6/17 10am PT call and walk through the YAML and SDK snippet.

Cheers,
Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding a couple operational notes: 

- Autoscale & reserved capacity: for the traffic profile you described we recommend a Dedicated pool with burst capacity for predictable p95 SLAs. We can propose a commit that covers baseline qps and burst credit for spikes.
- Cost/latency policy enforcement: we can run a policy simulator on historical traces to estimate cost impact of different fallback chains. That will help Acme pick the right defaults.
- Region failover: we'll enforce US-only by default and allow a soft-failover policy for secondary region if latency is still within your target. We'll document the exact behavior in the MAP.

I'll be on the Thu 6/17 10am PT deep-dive and can bring cost simulations.

Marcus
Director, Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference
